builder_plan.scenario: An agent looks good in demos, but you cannot tell which product tasks it fails.
builder_plan.change: Use the study's evaluation idea to inspect a small set of tasks with human-checked answers.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current evaluator and a manually reviewed reference set.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Agreement with human review, missed failures, false alarms, and evaluation cost per task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: LProp: Propagating Latent Uncertainty through Evidence-Conditioned Belief Revision in LLM Agents
summary: LProp replaces passing scalar confidence scores or verbose textual reflections between agent stages with compact latent-space uncertainty representations, and revises downstream answer distributions as new evidence arrives without extra trajectory sampling. The cost is the need for access to model internals (hidden states), which rules out closed third-party APIs, plus added pipeline complexity and an estimator component that must be trained or fitted. It can fail when the latent estimator miscalibrates on out-of-distribution tasks, when upstream errors are too severe for belief revision to recover, or when the reader's production models are API-only, making the method inapplicable.
rationale: The technique is directly relevant to multi-step agent pipelines on small open models, but it requires access to internal latent representations, so its gains must be validated on the reader's specific stack before adoption.
technique: Latent uncertainty propagation with evidence-conditioned belief revision

claims.statement: LProp replaces passing scalar confidence scores or verbose textual reflections between agent stages with compact latent-space uncertainty representations, and revises downstream answer distributions as new evidence arrives without extra trajectory sampling. The cost is the need for access to model internals (hidden states), which rules out closed third-party APIs, plus added pipeline complexity and an estimator component that must be trained or fitted. It can fail when the latent estimator miscalibrates on out-of-distribution tasks, when upstream errors are too severe for belief revision to recover, or when the reader's production models are API-only, making the method inapplicable.
LProp achieves the lowest mean inference-token usage across all eight evaluated propagation settings and outperforms baselines on most metrics, without additional trajectory sampling.
